title: Systematic discovery and perturbation of regulatory genes in human T cells reveals the architecture of immune networks
model: Primary human CD4+ T cells (3 donors), ~1,350-gene transcription-factor and immune-regulator knockout library, CD25 FACS sort
contrast: CD25 (IL2RA) high vs low bin, paired by donor (3 vs 3)
paper_calls: 58 genes at FDR 0.10 in the IL2RA screen (51 'significant hits' in the text); MED12, CBFB, KLF2, TNFAIP3, ZNF217, FOXK1 negative and STAT5A/B, JAK3, IRF4 positive regulators
barcs_calls: 126 genes at FDR 0.10 (65 up, 61 down in CD25-high); 133 against the control null centred on the targeting guides
named_hits: 13/13 at FDR 0.10; two-sided ranks: MED12 #1, CBFB #2, HIVEP2 #3, STAT5B #5, IL2RA #6, KLF2 #7, FOXK1 #9, ZNF217 #11, TNFAIP3 #12, STAT5A #19, JAK3 #26, IRF4 #64, ATXN7L3 #68 of 1,350
verdict: BARCS recovers all 58 of the authors' MAGeCK calls and every named regulator, with the IL2RA positive control at #6. It adds 68 smaller but guide-consistent effects, such as RUNX3, BCL11B and LEF1, that MAGeCK's permutation floor and unpaired ranking leave out.
